claim: The follicle stem cells (FSCs) in the Drosophila ovary are an important experimental model for the study of epithelial stem cell biology.
source: The follicle stem cells (FSCs) in the Drosophila ovary are an important experimental model for the study of epithelial stem cell biology.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus about the FSC model system.

claim: Decades of research support the conclusion that there are two FSCs per ovariole.
source: Although decades of research support the conclusion that there are two FSCs per ovariole, a recent study used a novel clonal marking system to conclude that there are 15–16 FSCs per ovariole.
evidence: This references the body of prior research literature supporting the two FSC model.

claim: A recent study concluded that there are 15–16 FSCs per ovariole using a novel clonal marking system.
source: Although decades of research support the conclusion that there are two FSCs per ovariole, a recent study used a novel clonal marking system to conclude that there are 15–16 FSCs per ovariole.
evidence: This cites the findings from Reilein et al., 2017.

claim: The authors identified several problems that may have contributed to the overestimate of FSC number in the Reilein et al. study.
source: We performed clonal analysis using both this novel clonal marking system and standard clonal marking systems, and identified several problems that may have contributed to the overestimate of FSC number.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data and analysis presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: FSC clones produce, on average, half of the follicle cells in each ovariole.
source: In addition, we developed new methods for accurately measuring clone size, and found that FSC clones produce, on average, half of the follicle cells in each ovariole.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative clone size measurements presented in Figure 4.

claim: There are typically two active FSCs per ovariole.
source: Our findings provide strong independent support for the conclusion that there are typically two active FSCs per ovariole, though they are consistent with up to four FSCs per germarium.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the clone size data and analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The findings are consistent with up to four FSCs per germarium.
source: Our findings provide strong independent support for the conclusion that there are typically two active FSCs per ovariole, though they are consistent with up to four FSCs per germarium.
evidence: This is based on the variability observed in clone sizes and patterns.

claim: The follicle epithelium of the Drosophila ovary has been a widely used and informative model for understanding epithelial tissue biology within the native, in vivo, environment.
source: The follicle epithelium of the Drosophila ovary has been a widely used and informative model for understanding epithelial tissue biology within the native, in vivo, environment (Sahai-Hernandez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The follicle epithelium was first described over 60 years ago as a single layered epithelium that encapsulates developing germ cell cysts.
source: First described over 60 years ago as a single layered epithelium that encapsulates developing germ cell cysts (Demerec, 1950; King et al., 1956), studies of this tissue have revealed insights into many aspects of epithelial biology
evidence: This is supported by citations to historical literature.

claim: Studies of the follicle epithelium have revealed insights into diverse mechanisms that regulate the specification of cell fate in an epithelial stem cell lineage.
source: studies of this tissue have revealed insights into many aspects of epithelial biology, including diverse mechanisms that regulate the specification of cell fate in an epithelial stem cell lineage (Assa-Kunik et al., 2007; Chang et al., 2013; González-Reyes and St Johnston, 1998; Johnston et al., 2016; Pocha and Montell, 2014; Song and Xie, 2003)
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Studies of the follicle epithelium have revealed insights into the establishment and maintenance of cell polarity.

claim: Studies of the follicle epithelium led to the discovery of a novel mechanism for establishing planar polarity.
source: and the discovery of a novel mechanism for establishing planar polarity (Cetera et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The Drosophila ovary has a highly consistent and well-described organization that facilitates the study of tissue biology with precise spatial and temporal resolution.
source: A distinct advantage of the Drosophila ovary as an experimental model is that it has a highly consistent and well-described organization that facilitates the study of tissue biology with precise spatial and temporal resolution.

claim: Each Drosophila ovary is composed of long chains of developing follicles, called ovarioles.

source: and oogenesis begins at the anterior tip of each ovariole in a structure called the germarium (Koch and King, 1966).

claim: GSCs divide during adulthood to self-renew and produce daughter cells called cystoblasts.
source: and divide during adulthood to self-renew and produce daughter cells called cystoblasts.
